description:
`#fn<a/b>` reports arity in `b` (fz-gk4) but `a` is still `closure_schema_id` --
the id of an interned `ClosureEnv{n}` schema, minted in ALLOCATION ORDER and
keyed only by CAPTURE COUNT:

    runtime/src/heap/imp.rs:199
      pub(crate) fn closure_schema_id(&mut self, captured_count: usize) -> u32 {
          self.schemas.borrow_mut().closure_env(captured_count)
      }

Every ordinary closure routes through it via `alloc_closure_slots`
(imp.rs:608-611).

## Three consequences, all reproduced at HEAD

1. IDENTITY DOES NOT DISTINGUISH. Two different closures with the same capture
   count render the same leading id.

       $ ./target/debug/fz2 run fixtures2/behavior/closure_render_arity.fz
       #fn<2/0>
       #fn<2/2>

   Both capture `total`; only the arity slot tells them apart.

2. INTERP AND NATIVE DISAGREE for the same program.

       $ ./target/debug/fz2 interp fixtures2/behavior/closure_render_arity.fz
       #fn<3/0>
       #fn<3/2>

   The fixture therefore carries a `.expected.interp.txt` whose ONLY difference
   from `.expected.txt` is this leading id.

3. IT IS FRAGILE AGAINST UNRELATED CHANGES. Removing one unrelated interpreter
   tuple allocation in fz-66j renumbered enum_reduce_suspend::interp from
   `#fn<3/0>` to `#fn<2/0>`. This golden has been re-blessed in this slot twice
   in one week (fz-gk4, then fz-66j). Each re-bless records nothing about the
   program.

## Elixir's answer

Elixir's leading component is `new_index.uniq` -- the fun's SOURCE-ORDER index
plus a module-code hash -- so it is source-derived, stable across runs, and it
distinguishes:

    total = Enum.reduce([1,2,3], 0, fn x, acc -> x + acc end)
    nullary = fn -> total end
    binary = fn x, y -> x + y + total end
    IO.inspect(nullary); IO.inspect(binary)

    #Function<1.88208959 in file:/tmp/cr.exs>
    #Function<2.88208959 in file:/tmp/cr.exs>

Index 1 vs 2 (source order), shared module hash. Reference:
../elixir/lib/elixir/lib/inspect.ex:589.

## Direction

Make the env schema per closure SITE rather than per capture count.
`Heap::alloc_closure_slots_with_schema` (runtime/src/heap/imp.rs:622) already
accepts a verbatim schema id, and a per-site schema is what a closure environment
actually IS -- this REMOVES the capture-count bucket rather than adding a
concept. The callable-boundary id is the natural source-order key and is in hand
at every construction site.

RESEARCH FIRST: the doc comment at imp.rs:614-621 warns that registering
per-site schemas perturbs the schema-id space the AOT runtime must keep
byte-identical to compile time, and that both the interpreter and codegen render
it. Size that before committing.

## What the old ticket got wrong

Its acceptance said "enum_reduce_suspend and closure_render_arity each drop to a
single golden". Only closure_render_arity does. enum_reduce_suspend's two goldens
differ in a SECOND, unrelated way:

    < {:suspended, 0, #fn<4/0>}
    < {3, 48, 1, 48, 1, 48, 0, 0}
    ---
    > {:suspended, 0, #fn<2/0>}
    > {3, 48, 1, 48, 2, 64, 0, 0}

Line 2 is closure_allocs 1 vs 2 / closure_bytes 48 vs 64 -- a real interp/native
allocation contract difference the fixture header documents. That fixture keeps
two goldens regardless of this fix.

## Checks

- The leading slot derives from the closure's source identity (callable-boundary
  id), not from allocation order or capture count.
- `closure_render_arity` renders two DIFFERENT leading ids for its two closures,
  matching Elixir's index-distinguishes property.
- interp and native agree on the leading id;
  `closure_render_arity.expected.interp.txt` is deleted and the fixture runs on
  one golden.
- enum_reduce_suspend's remaining golden divergence is allocation counts ONLY.
- AOT: schema ids stay byte-identical between compile time and runtime; full
  matrix green on run/interp/build.
title: Rendered closure identity is an allocation-order env-schema id keyed by capture count, not a source-derived fun index
